title: Grateful Dead Live at Winterland Arena on 1973-11-10

ai_review.summary: Soundboard source with noticeable pitch‑speed issues, but a thrilling second‑set sandwich (Playin' → Uncle John’s → Morning Dew) that makes the show worth listening to.
ai_review.review: The recording is a soundboard capture that suffers from a half‑step fast‑up pitch and occasional level spikes, especially around the U.J.B. segment, making it a bit rough technically. Musically the concert shines in the second set – the extended Playin' > Uncle John’s > Morning Dew sequence is repeatedly praised as “smoking” and “breathtaking,” while the first set is viewed as uneven but still contains highlights like Jack Straw and Bertha.

ai_rating.rationale: Average star rating ≈3.7, but detailed positive comments about the second‑set jam outweigh the technical complaints; many reviewers give 4–5 stars and describe the music as exceptional.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Pitch runs roughly a half‑step high (≈+5 % speed), noticeable wow & flutter on cassette source, occasional volume spikes at the U.J.B. section, but overall intelligible and balanced mix.

poor_songs: First‑set material (early songs) – described as sluggish or lackluster
show_quality.setlist_flow: The first set builds slowly and is uneven, but gains momentum around Deal and Mexicali. The second set erupts into a marathon jam sandwich that carries the concert’s energy.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly described as ‘raging’, delivering masterful swirls, perfect tone, and hot soloing throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob (Bobby) noted for solid rhythm work and “mind‑meld” moments on Big River; occasional vocal strain later in the set.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s cascading keyboard riffs highlighted during Wharf Rat; overall keyboards praised for adding texture.
